title: Report failure causes and bound infrastructure replacements
body:
An infrastructure interruption can stop healthy task code and consume an ordinary retry. This combined prototype reports failure causes to listeners and metrics, and lets administrators grant bounded replacement attempts for confirmed infrastructure failures.

`[core] max_infra_retries` defaults to `0`; Dag authors get no new parameter. The policy reuses existing retry fields without a migration or an AIP-103 counter. Ordinary attempts and clears can exhaust the allowance early. Raising ordinary retries can reopen an early refusal, but not once the prior-attempt count reaches the cap. Unclassified failures do not qualify.

This implements the combined reference for [AIP-97 classification](https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/spaces/AIRFLOW/pages/399279312/AIP-97+Task+Failure+Classification) and [AIP-116 bounded infrastructure retries](https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/spaces/AIRFLOW/pages/451974654/AIP-116+Bounded+Infrastructure+Retries). Classification is independently reviewable in https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/73350.

## Testing Done

Real Kubernetes Task SDK workers made authenticated starts and later heartbeats before interruption. PostgreSQL snapshots, listener records, callbacks, and UDP metrics showed:

| Scenario | Default cap 0 | Cap 1 |
|---|---|---|
| Confirmed taint-manager interruption, `retries=0` | Failed on attempt 1 | Succeeded on attempt 2; one grant |
| Workload storage-limit eviction | Failed, unclassified | Same; no grant |
| Application, timeout, and manual controls | Failed without replacement | Same |
| Ordinary retry followed by a clear | Attempts 1, 2, 3; callbacks `retry`, `success`, `success` | Same |

The [runnable workflow, complete fixture, provenance, and sanitized evidence](https://gist.github.com/1fanwang/8e64336d1e879fe6021a72b82d895f3a/ccbc40261f60708683bf3732aa403d771ed05a13) include setup. These commands ran on Linux:

```bash
SOURCE_SHA=77b67ade969b160f7550437e6b5108926d3ecc15
flags=(--policy)
python fixture/run.py --source "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/source" --commit "$SOURCE_SHA" "${flags[@]}"
runs=(fixture/runs/*)
python fixture/verify_evidence.py "${runs[0]}" --candidate "$SOURCE_SHA" "${flags[@]}"
```

+``on_task_instance_failed`` can receive a :class:`~airflow_shared.state.TaskFailureKind`:

+``Evicted`` or ``WorkerLost``. A reason can be present without a failure kind.
+
+.. code-block:: python

+    @hookimpl
+    def on_task_instance_failed(self, previous_state, task_instance, error, failure_kind, reason):
+        if failure_kind == "infra":
+            record_infrastructure_disruption(reason)
+
+The enum inherits from ``str`` and compares equal to its lower-case value. Existing listeners

@@ -166,6 +166,41 @@ If you want to control your task's state from within custom Task/Operator code,
 
 These can be useful if your code has extra knowledge about its environment and wants to fail/skip faster - e.g., skipping when it knows there's no data available, or fast-failing when it detects its API key is invalid (as that will not be fixed by a retry).
 
+Infrastructure replacement attempts
+-----------------------------------
+
+Administrators can set :ref:`config:core__max_infra_retries` to grant additional attempts when an
+executor confirms that infrastructure stopped a task. The default is ``0``, which disables
+replacement attempts. No Dag or task setting is required, including for tasks with ``retries=0``.
+An unknown cause, generic worker loss, or a missed heartbeat does not qualify.
+
+The scheduler locks and refreshes the task instance before handling an executor failure. Only a
+``RUNNING`` task can receive a replacement; queued, cleared and already-handled states do not
+produce an infrastructure policy decision. The scheduler increases the existing ``max_tries``
+before deciding the retry state, callback, and email notification. For each running failure it
+recomputes ``max((max_tries or 0) - (retries or 0), try_number - 1, 0)`` and grants a replacement
+only if that inferred position is below ``max_infra_retries``.
+
+This is a conservative ceiling rather than a separate count of infrastructure failures. Ordinary
+attempts and task clears can consume the allowance without any infrastructure replacement. An early
+refusal can change after normal retries are edited, because ``max_tries - retries`` can decrease.
+Once ``try_number - 1`` reaches the configured cap, neither clears nor normal-retry edits can
+restore eligibility under that same cap. These persisted fields survive scheduler restarts.
+After a refusal, normal retry handling still applies.
+
+Kubernetes ``Evicted`` alone does not qualify: the same pod reason is used for workload storage-limit
+violations. A documented disruption condition can supply the missing evidence. Container termination
+reasons are retained for diagnosis but are not matched against pod-level infrastructure reasons.
+
+``ti_infra_retry_granted`` counts granted replacements, and ``ti_infra_retry_denied`` counts
+confirmed running infrastructure failures refused by the enabled policy's current ceiling. Neither increments
+when the policy is disabled or the cause is not infrastructure. These named counters also work
+with plain StatsD. Tagged backends add a bounded ``failure_kind`` to ``ti_failures`` and
+``operator_failures``; an unset cause is labeled ``unclassified`` for metrics only.
+
+Failure listeners receive the optional cause and backend reason even when replacement attempts
+are disabled. Dag callbacks keep their existing context API. See :doc:`/administration-and-deployment/listeners`.
+

+    task: Operator | None,
+    failure_kind: TaskFailureKind | None,
+    reason: str | None = None,

+    """Grant a replacement for a running failure within the deployment's inferred ceiling."""
+    if failure_kind != TaskFailureKind.INFRA or task is None:
+        return False
+
+    infra_retries = conf.getint("core", "max_infra_retries", fallback=0)
